justifications.fit: The mechanism comments state the rule (the descriptor is written only after the registry holds the version; the mkstemp+os.replace write is atomic for a concurrent reader and an interrupted write; the replacement keeps the descriptor's own permission bits through stat.S_IMODE) with no plan, ticket or phase reference. The module idiom -- typed click command, mechanism docstrings, module-level regex, EXCLUDED_TOP_LEVEL filter, _BUNDLE_TEMP_RE following _SEMVER_RE -- is preserved, and ruff exits 0 at head.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The plan section's follow-on (from the review of the failed-push repair): stop `release` writing the local bundle.json before the push and make that write atomic, and close the two follow-ons the prior reviews left. Fully met at 8af5104d/607add49: imas_ambix/maps_cli.py release() stages and pushes inside the TemporaryDirectory block and calls write_released_version only after push_tree returns (line 495), so nothing local names an unpublished version and there is no byte-restore to get wrong; _write_bundle_version writes a sibling temp and moves it over the descriptor with os.replace; the replacement takes the descriptor's own permission bits through stat.S_IMODE, so mkstemp's 0600 does not become the published mode and no file-type bits reach os.chmod (the prior info finding is now closed); and released_paths leaves out a stray bundle.json.*.tmp so a process killed mid-write cannot put it into the digest or the staged tree. The tests extend the existing FakeRegistry and push_tree stubbing rather than introducing a new fake, and the during-push test reuses the stubbed push_tree to observe the descriptor mid-push.
justifications.scope_discipline: The three changed paths -- imas_ambix/maps_cli.py, tests/test_maps_cli.py and the section's landing fragment under docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-facility-mint/ -- sit inside the node's declared write paths and the plan §18 release CLI surface; no other command, module or plan file is touched.
